title: Pointwise criterion for a nodal singularity by the first Fitting ideal
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $x$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points]. Let $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(C/k)$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Say that $x$ is a node when, for an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and some point $\bar x$ of the base change $C_{\bar k}$ [def-pc-base-change] over $x$, the completed local ring (the $\mathfrak m_{\bar x}$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of $\mathcal O_{C_{\bar k},\bar x}$) is isomorphic to $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] (the completed geometric local-ring condition of [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]). Then $x$ is a node if and only if the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a finite separable algebraic extension of $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra that is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], and $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=\kappa(x)$ (equivalently, the first Fitting ideal of the relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] generates the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{C,x}$).

source.place: Tags 0C4D (lemma-nodal), 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), and 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), pointwise form at a closed point

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $S$ is finite type over $k$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] to write $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}=S_{\mathfrak p}$, $F=S/\mathfrak p$, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$. By [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], with $J_A=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{S/k})A$ (the localization clause there), the stalk $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ is $A/J_A$ (zero when $x\notin Z$). Hence $\mathcal O_{Z,x}=F$ via the residue map means exactly $J_A=\mathfrak m$, and in particular it forces $x\in Z$. The open base-change and affine fibre-product identifications [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify a geometric stalk over $x$ with $B=(S\otimes_k\bar k)_{\mathfrak q}$; [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent] gives its residue field $\bar k$.

If $x$ is a node, apply [lem-trf-geometric-node-fitting-depth] to its chosen geometric stalk: $J_B=\mathfrak m_B$ and $\operatorname{depth}B=1$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-fitting-depth-descent] to obtain finite separability of $F/k$, $J_A=\mathfrak m$, and depth one for $A$.

The conditions just obtained satisfy [lem-trf-depth-fitting-quadratic-lci]. Choose its $g\notin\mathfrak p$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}S_g\subseteq U$ is an affine LCI neighbourhood of $x$, completing the forward implication.

Conversely, choose the assumed affine LCI neighbourhood. By [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], pure dimension one gives dimension at $x$ equal to one; [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] give $\dim A=1$. By [lem-trf-completion-local-complete-intersection], $\operatorname{depth}A=\dim A=1$. Finite separability and $J_A=\mathfrak m$ are hypotheses, so [lem-trf-depth-fitting-quadratic-lci] gives a quadratic completion with a $k$-algebra coefficient section and nonzero discriminant.

Choose a geometric lift by [lem-trf-geometric-field-stalk-descent]. It is a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S\otimes_k\bar k$ over $\mathfrak p$ with $(S\otimes_k\bar k)/\mathfrak q=\bar k$; the induced map $F=S/\mathfrak p\to\bar k$ is a $k$-embedding $\iota$, and $\mathfrak q$ is the kernel of $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\iota(\bar s)\lambda$, since that map is the quotient map. By step 1, $B=(S\otimes_k\bar k)_{\mathfrak q}$ is the local ring of a point of $C_{\bar k}$ over $x$. Apply [lem-trf-quadratic-completion-geometric-splitting] to the quadratic completion from the preceding step. It gives $\widehat B\cong\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$, which is the required node condition.

lean.statement: theorem nodalPoint_iff_separable_lci_firstFitting {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hpure : C.IsPureDimension 1) (x : C) (hx : x ∈ closedPoints C) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosure k Ω] : (∃ y : pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))), pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω))) y = x ∧ Nonempty (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))).presheaf.stalk y)) ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Ω)))).presheaf.stalk y) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) Ω ⧸ Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) Ω) * (MvPowerSeries.X 1 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) Ω)}))) ↔ (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x).Finite ∧ @Algebra.IsSeparable k (C.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x).toAlgebra ∧ ∃ (U : C.affineOpens) (hxU : x ∈ U.1) (hfg : @Algebra.FiniteType k Γ(C, U.1) _ _ ((f.appLE ⊤ U.1 le_top).hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom).toAlgebra), @Algebra.IsLocalCompleteIntersection k Γ(C, U.1) _ _ ((f.appLE ⊤ U.1 le_top).hom.comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom).toAlgebra hfg ∧ ((Scheme.firstFittingIdealSheaf f).ideal U).map (C.presheaf.germ U.1 x hxU).hom = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk x)
